gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 expands only with the Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 (up to five packs, about 11 kWh), or that first-generation Battery Pack 2000 Plus and Battery Pack 1000 Plus units will not work with it.
standout_why: I compared against GearBrain's HomePower 1000 Plus v2 review, which says 'up to approximately 11kWh with optional 2kWh expansion batteries' but names no pack model and no maximum count. It tells buyers to confirm 'the exact number of supported expansion batteries, compatible battery model' themselves. Notebookcheck's Explorer 1500 Ultra article and the TechRadar headline (the body was truncated) do not mention expansion at all. The Notebookcheck 1000 v2 page and ProToolReviews could not be checked: ProToolReviews returned HTTP 403 and I did not open the Notebookcheck 1000 v2 page. None of the pages I read names the v2-only pack lock, and none says the Explorer 1000 v2 cannot expand.
decides: This settles the expandable-versus-fixed choice. A shopper who wants to add capacity later should buy the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (or the HomePower 2000 Plus v2) and budget for the Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 specifically. A first-generation Battery Pack 2000 Plus or 1000 Plus from the used or clearance market will not work with it. The Explorer 1000 v2 is the fixed-capacity pick: it takes no expansion pack, and the Explorer 1000 Plus pack does not fit it. Jackery's transfer switches are listed against the 5000 Plus and the HomePower 3600 Pro Max, not the 1000-class units. A shopper who wants a home transfer switch should therefore look higher in the range.

findings.label: Compatible expansion battery
findings.value: Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 only. Battery Pack 2000 Plus (1st gen) and Battery Pack 1000 Plus are not compatible.
findings.source_title: Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 Review: 1kWh to 11kWh, Built to Grow (2026), Dan Miller, BackupPowerHub
findings.note: Quoted: 'compatible only with the Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2… The Battery Pack 2000 Plus (first generation) and the Battery Pack 1000 Plus will not work with it, according to Jackery.' The page was last updated 2026-11-03. Jackery's US product page carries the same statement according to search results, but it returned HTTP 429 every time I tried to open it, so the maker wording is cited through this reviewer.

findings.label: Maximum expansion
findings.value: 5 × Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2, about 11 kWh total
findings.source_title: Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 Review: 1kWh to 11kWh, Built to Grow (2026), Dan Miller, BackupPowerHub
findings.note: Quoted: 'up to five Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 units, each adding 2kWh, for a maximum of 11kWh.' This matches Jackery's own series-page banner, 'Modular from 1024Wh to 11kWh' (https://www.jackery.com/products/homepower-1000-plus-v2-series, read 2026-11-15).

findings.label: Jackery's pack-to-station pairing labels
findings.value: Battery Pack 2000 Plus: 'Compatible with 2000 Plus'. Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2: 'Compatible with HomePower 2000 Plus v2'. Battery Pack 5000 Plus: 'Compatible with 5000 Plus'. Battery Pack 3600: 'Compatible with Homepower 3600 Plus'.
findings.source_title: How Big Can Jackery Plus Get? Expandable Power and Capacity Breakdown (Jackery)
findings.note: These come from the product cards on Jackery's own page. The article body was truncated, so no maximum pack counts were visible there.

findings.label: Expansion battery compatibility
findings.value: Not compatible with the Explorer 1000 Plus Battery Pack. No expansion pack is listed.
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000v2 1070Wh Portable Power Station (Not compatible with Explorer 1000 Plus Battery Pack), Mr. Solar
findings.note: This is retailer wording. The Solar Lab's review (https://www.thesolarlab.com/review/jackery-1000-v2-review, read 2026-11-15) also states 'the battery is not expandable' and points to the 1000 Plus as the expandable alternative. Jackery's AU page returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Solar/DC input limits
findings.value: 2 × DC8020: 12–16 V ⎓ 8 A / 16–60 V ⎓ 10.5 A, 400 W max combined. Car input 12 V / 10 A.
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000v2 1070Wh Portable Power Station, Mr. Solar
findings.note: The Solar Lab describes the inputs as 'Dual MC3 connectors' for 400 W combined. The connector naming conflicts between the two sources, but both give a 400 W ceiling. The Solar Lab also says Jackery advertises 600 W with six panels while the unit label lists 400 W max.

findings.label: Transfer switch pairings
findings.value: Smart Transfer Switch: 'Compatible with 5000 Plus'. Manual Transfer Switch: 'Compatible with HomePower 3600 Pro Max'.
findings.note: These are the accessory cards on Jackery's own series page. No transfer switch is listed for the HomePower 1000 Plus v2.
